target.what: Total number of tokens processed (input plus output, including cached and reasoning tokens where applicable) by all large language models worldwide during calendar year 2025, aggregated across both provider-operated consumer/enterprise products (chat apps, coding assistants, embedded features) and t
target.publisher: None — no single official publisher exists; would require synthesis across provider disclosures (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, ByteDance, Alibaba, DeepSeek, xAI, Mistral, etc.) and third-party trackers (OpenRouter, Poe, Artificial Analysis, Similarweb, a16z, Epoch AI).

target.caveats: Working interpretation: worldwide, all providers, full calendar year 2025, tokens = input + output tokens billed/processed at inference (including cached input and reasoning tokens). Alternatives that would materially change the answer: (a) API-only vs. API+first-party products (first-party consumer

candidates.perspective: Hyperscaler / frontier-lab disclosures (Google, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, ByteDance, Alibaba)
candidates.hypothesis: Several major providers periodically disclose aggregate token throughput (e.g., Google's 'X trillion tokens per month' for Gemini API, Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry token counts, Meta's Llama token stats). Summing disclosed monthly/quarterly rates across the largest providers, then scaling up for the long tail of smaller providers, yields a bottom-up global total. Direction: higher disclosed rates → higher total; coverage gap is the main uncertainty.
candidates.data_to_find: Any provider-published token-per-month or token-per-quarter figures covering any part of 2025 (Google Gemini API, Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, ByteDance Doubao, Alibaba Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral). Minimum: at least 3-4 large-provider datapoints with dates, plus an estimate of each provider's share of global volume to bridge to the total.
search_hints: Google Gemini API trillion tokens per month 2025
Azure AI Foundry tokens processed monthly 2025

candidates.perspective: Third-party API aggregators and routers (OpenRouter, Poe, Together, Fireworks, Groq)
candidates.hypothesis: OpenRouter publishes weekly token totals across its marketplace; scaling OpenRouter's share of global API token volume (estimated via revenue or request share) gives an API-segment total. API segment is a minority of total tokens but more observable. Direction: higher OpenRouter volume → higher API total; share assumption is the key transfer.
candidates.data_to_find: OpenRouter weekly/monthly token totals for 2025 (they publish rankings and sometimes aggregate tokens), plus any estimate of OpenRouter's share of total API inference market (revenue or request share vs. direct provider APIs). Substitute: Poe or Together AI disclosed volumes.

candidates.perspective: Datacenter / GPU capacity and utilisation (NVIDIA shipments, hyperscaler capex, inference vs. training split)
candidates.hypothesis: Global inference token throughput is bounded by deployed inference compute: (GPU fleet dedicated to inference) × (tokens/sec per GPU at realistic batch/utilisation) × (seconds in year). This gives an upper bound and, with an inference-share and utilisation assumption, a central estimate. Direction: more inference GPUs and higher utilisation → more tokens.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 NVIDIA/AMD datacenter GPU shipments or installed base; hyperscaler capex split between training and inference; published tokens/sec per GPU (e.g., H100/H200/B200 inference benchmarks at production batch sizes); average utilisation of inference fleets. Minimum: an inference-GPU count and a tokens/sec-per-GPU figure.
search_hints: NVIDIA data center GPU shipments 2025 inference
H100 tokens per second inference benchmark batch

candidates.perspective: Energy / power draw of AI datacenters as a proxy for inference work
candidates.hypothesis: AI datacenter electricity consumption in 2025, split into inference vs. training, converted via energy-per-token (joules/token) benchmarks, yields a token total. Direction: higher AI datacenter power and higher inference share → more tokens; energy-per-token is the conversion factor with wide uncertainty.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 AI datacenter power consumption estimates (IEA, EPRI, SemiAnalysis, LBNL), inference share of AI compute, and published joules-per-token figures (e.g., from Epoch AI, Google, or academic measurements). Minimum: an inference-energy total and a joules/token range.
search_hints: AI data center electricity consumption 2025 IEA
joules per token LLM inference energy

candidates.perspective: User-base × usage decomposition (ChatGPT/Gemini/Meta AI/Claude weekly actives × messages × tokens per message)
candidates.hypothesis: Total tokens ≈ Σ over products (weekly/monthly active users × sessions or messages per user × tokens per message, including context). Provider user disclosures (OpenAI 800M weekly, Meta AI 1B+, Gemini app users) combined with average tokens-per-request benchmarks give a first-party-product total; API adds a separate component. Direction: more users and longer contexts → more tokens.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 user/usage disclosures for major consumer LLM products (ChatGPT weekly actives, Gemini app MAU, Meta AI MAU, Claude, Copilot, Doubao, Qwen app), average messages per user per day, and average tokens per request (input+output, including system prompt and context). Minimum: 2-3 large products' user counts plus a tokens-per-request benchmark.

candidates.perspective: Token-per-request and context-length benchmarks (Artificial Analysis, provider docs, academic measurement)
candidates.hypothesis: The tokens-per-interaction conversion factor (input context + output, including reasoning) is needed by d5 and d1. Longer contexts and reasoning models raise tokens per request substantially in 2025. Direction: higher measured tokens/request → higher totals from any user- or request-based route.
candidates.data_to_find: Measured average input and output tokens per request for major models/products in 2025 (Artificial Analysis, OpenRouter per-model token stats, provider usage dashboards, academic studies). Minimum: a range for chat-style and coding-agent-style requests, plus reasoning-token multipliers.
search_hints: average input output tokens per LLM request 2025

candidates.perspective: Analyst forecasts and market-sizing reports on AI inference / token volume
candidates.hypothesis: Research firms (Epoch AI, a16z, Menlo Ventures, IDC, Gartner, SemiAnalysis) publish estimates of total inference tokens or inference compute for 2025. These provide an independent cross-check or a direct figure. Direction: forecasters' central estimates anchor the range; check whether they cover API only or all usage.
candidates.data_to_find: Published 2025 estimates of global LLM token volume or inference compute (Epoch AI token-throughput estimates, Menlo Ventures enterprise LLM API spend/tokens, a16z, IDC). Minimum: one or two independent aggregate estimates with stated scope.
search_hints: Menlo Ventures LLM API token volume 2025

candidates.perspective: Time series of disclosed token growth to extrapolate 2025 from earlier anchors
candidates.hypothesis: Where providers disclosed token volumes in 2023-2024 (e.g., Google's progression from 9.7T to 480T tokens/month, Microsoft's Azure OpenAI token growth), fitting growth curves and extrapolating through 2025 constrains the total. Direction: faster observed growth → higher 2025 total.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical token-volume disclosures for 2023-2024 and any 2025 partials (Google Gemini API monthly tokens, Azure OpenAI/Foundry tokens, OpenAI usage stats), aligned by date, to fit growth and extrapolate to full-year 2025. Minimum: 2-3 dated datapoints per major provider.

assessment.note: Same Microsoft Azure/Foundry quarterly figure (~100T tokens, up 5x YoY, record 50T month) reported by three outlets; they share one underlying Microsoft disclosure, so this is one measurement, not three.
Same 'record 50T tokens in one month' Microsoft statement, duplicated across sources; single underlying disclosure.
Google's 480T tokens/month (April/May 2025) figure repeated across outlets; one Google disclosure.
Google's ~980T tokens/month (July 2025) figure, duplicated; single disclosure.
Google daily rate ~32.7T/day is consistent with ~980T/month; both derive from the same Google throughput disclosure.
Google all-surfaces monthly token counts at successive dates (1.3Q/month Q3 2025; 3.2Q/month May 2026) form a consistent growth trajectory with p6/p196.

API-only throughput disclosures (Google 7B→10B tokens/min; OpenAI 6B tokens/min ≈ 8.6T/day) are mutually consistent in order of magnitude and show API is a minority of total tokens versus first-party surfaces.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
